messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Error Stream
parts: I just want to confirm the new format for error handling.  Have all exceptions been removed in lieu of adding an error stream, or is the error stream in addition to the exceptions?  In particular, I'm thinking about how to call model::grad_log_prob properly.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Error Stream
parts:
On 4/28/13 12:52 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> I just want to confirm the new format for error handling.
> Have all exceptions been removed in lieu of adding an error stream,
> or is the error stream in addition to the exceptions?

> In particular, I'm thinking about how to call model::grad_log_prob properly.

The error handling in C++ now has a global configuration.
You can configure error handling to return NaN or
to throw exceptions (among other things).

We've configured the Stan modeling language to throw
exceptions.

The way we've dealt with calls to grad_log_prob is to
catch exceptions, print their messages to the error
stream, then treat it as a -infinity log probability.
NaN should be treated the same way (you can still get
NaN returns from std lib calls and some of our own that
we haven't added error checking policies to).

This combination of exceptions plus catch around calls
to log_prob lets us get an informative message
back to the user while still rejecting the parameter
state.

- Bob
